subject: Pilot-fit digest: candidate models, perf snapshots, prompt bank, and regression plan
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lee Tan <lee@orbisai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-03T14:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot-fit digest: candidate models, perf snapshots, prompt bank, and regression plan

Thanks for the call earlier, Lee — good discussion and really helpful context on the throughput targets (20 TPS for synchronous chat, 200k msgs/day) and the strict latency budget for search augmentation (p99 < 450ms). Quick recap and recommended next steps below so we have a single source of truth for the pilot kick-off.

Summary of ask:
- Production pilot to validate retrieval-augmented generation for search answers and short-form summarization.
- Latency targets: p99 end-to-end for single-turn generation < 450ms in us-west; cost target ~ $0.0008 per request (goal).
- Data: 1M documents, retrieval layer external to Redwood.

Redwood pilot-fit recommendations (high level):
1) Candidate model slate (fast shortlist for pilot):
   - Redwood-Compact-3B-q4: best-in-class cost/latency for chat fallback (single-token latency optimized).
   - Redwood-13B-fp16: quality-first option for summarization; higher cost but better faithfulness on long context.
   - Llama2-13B-q4-rev1 (community): lowest-cost variant we can route to as a fallthrough for degraded capacity.

2) Verified perf snapshots (attached & link below):
   - Redwood-Compact-3B-q4 (seq512, batch=8): 140 TPS sustained, token p50=6ms, p95=18ms, p99=38ms on an A100-equivalent node.
   - Redwood-13B-fp16 (seq1024, batch=4): 48 TPS sustained, token p50=18ms, p95=45ms, p99=110ms.
   - Llama2-13B-q4 (seq512, batch=8): 110 TPS sustained, token p50=8ms, p95=26ms, p99=60ms.

3) Quality/regression guardrails we recommend for pilot:
   - Baseline prompt pack (attached) + 200 evaluation prompts we use as a regression harness.
   - Automated evals: BLEU/ROUGE for template outputs, hallucination checks with knowledge prompts, and a small human-in-the-loop review set for first 500 responses.
   - Alerting thresholds: >7% quality regression on the core promptset triggers rollback.

4) Operational & routing suggestions:
   - Start pilot pinned to Redwood-Compact-3B-q4 for primary traffic; enable auto-fallback to Llama2-13B-q4 if capacity constrained.
   - Enable prefix KV caching for repeated user prompts to reduce cost and improve p50.

Next steps:
- I attached the Redwood-verified performance profile for the slate plus the prompt pack and the raw bench traces.
- Proposed pilot kickoff: week of 10/18. Can you confirm availability for a 30-minute pilot scoping session next week (10/07 or 10/08)?

Thanks — I’ll loop engineering (Ben) into the scoping once we lock a time.

—
Alex Martinez
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com
attachments: redwood-perf-profile-orbis.pdf (PDF, 620KB), orbis-prompt-pack.csv (CSV, 24KB), bench-traces-20261003.json (JSON, 2.1MB)

Date: 2026-10-03T17:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot-fit digest: candidate models, perf snapshots, prompt bank, and regression plan

Thanks Alex — very clear, appreciate the numbers. A couple of quick clarifications from our side: 

1) For the p99 latency numbers you shared, are those token-level or end-to-end request p99s? Our SLA is end-to-end (retrieval + model) so we want to make sure the numbers map correctly.
2) On the regression threshold (7%), how do you compute that — token overlap vs. a reference human? We’re sensitive to precision for search answers.

Also — one non-negotiable for procurement is a formal perf profile that we can attach to the SOW. Can you provide a signed perf snapshot or a document we can include?

If we can get those answers by EOD Wednesday, we can confirm the 10/18 pilot window.

Lee
Head of AI Platforms, Orbis AI
lee@orbisai.com

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lee Tan <lee@orbisai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-04T10:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot-fit digest: candidate models, perf snapshots, prompt bank, and regression plan

Lee — great questions. Short answers up front, and I’ve attached the perf profile & bench traces you can attach to the SOW.

1) p99 definitions: the numbers in my first note are token-level latencies measured inside our runtime (kernel hop -> token emission). For end-to-end request p99 you should add retrieval time and network overhead. Based on your retrieval SLA (avg 120ms, p95 220ms), our estimated end-to-end p99 for Redwood-Compact-3B-q4 on your traffic shape is ~360–420ms (depends on batching and warm cache). I’ve included a worked example in the attached perf profile (see section B, page 4).

2) Regression metric: the 7% threshold is computed against our curated promptpack using a weighted quality score (0–100) that mixes lexical overlap (ROUGE) and semantic similarity (embedding cosine) and a manual adjudication weight for hallucination. We surface both absolute score deltas and per-prompt failure counts; the rollback rule is either >7% aggregate drop or >5% of prompts flagged for high-severity hallucinations. The perf profile has the exact math and sample calculations.

Attachments included (links below):
- perf profile (signed): redwood-perf-profile-orbis.pdf — includes tested hardware, kernel configs, batch sizing, and end-to-end worked examples.
- bench traces: bench-traces-20261003.json — raw traces from our test harness (seq/bs variations).
- prompt pack: orbis-prompt-pack.csv — baseline prompts we recommend for regression.

Quick pilot scoping items I’ll bring to the engineering sync with Ben:
- Desired steady-state concurrency and expected peak windows (please confirm expected 1-hour peak).
- Which model do you want to start pinned for pilot (Compact-3B or 13B)? My recommendation: start Compact-3B-q4 and flip to 13B-fp16 for the summarization route in the A/B branch.

Scheduling: I’m free 10/07 10–12pm PT or 10/08 2–4pm PT for a 30-minute scoping call. Which works for you?

—
Alex Martinez
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood-perf-profile-orbis.pdf (signed, 620KB), bench-traces-20261003.json (2.1MB), orbis-prompt-pack.csv (24KB)
